targets.semantic_primary: Let G be a binary tree. If the law of edge lengths has a tail that decays slower than exponentially, then Phi*_E(G) > 0 yet Phi*_E(G_nu) = 0 a.s., where G_nu is the Section 6.9 random subdivision.
targets.scope: The single a.s. conclusion of Exercise 6.88 for a binary tree with the root as basepoint and a subdivision law on the positive integers with no exponential tail: the anchored edge-expansion constant of the random subdivision is 0 a.s. The companion clause Phi*_E(G) > 0 is the standing positive-expansion property of the base tree and is not a second target; the necessity remark on physical p. 240 and Theorem 6.50 on physical p. 238 are the body statements this exercise is attached to and are not counted again.
ambient_hypotheses: G is a binary tree with root o used as basepoint, as printed in the exercise and in the opening sentence of the Comment.
The subdivision law nu is a probability distribution on the positive integers and the edge lengths are i.i.d. with law nu, exactly as the random subdivision is defined on physical p. 238.

The hypothesis is stated twice in the record in the author's two phrasings: the exercise says the tail "decays slower than exponentially" and the Comment says the distribution "does not have an exponential tail".

The index n in the Comment is the number of edges of a level-n-to-level-2n path and simultaneously the exponent of the count 2^n of such paths, as printed; the constant c and the accuracy epsilon are quantified as printed.

functional_definitions.binary tree: the rooted tree with two children at every vertex, with levels counted from the root o, as used in the exercise and in the Comment's collection of paths from level n to level 2n.
functional_definitions.random subdivision G_nu: physical p. 238: each edge e of G is replaced by a path of L_e >= 1 edges, the L_e i.i.d. with law nu, giving the random graph G_nu.
functional_definitions.exponential tail: physical p. 238: nu has an exponential tail if for some epsilon > 0 and all sufficiently large l we have nu[l, infinity) < e^{-epsilon l}; equivalently E[s^X] < infinity for some s > 1 when X has law nu.
functional_definitions.Phi*_E (anchored edge-expansion constant: physical p. 234: the limit as n grows of the infimum of |d_E K| / |K| over connected K containing o with n <= |K| < infinity.
functional_definitions.Phi**_E and E(K): physical pp. 217 and 238: the same infimum with denominator |E(K)|, where E(K) is the edge set printed as (6.33); for trees |E(K)| = |K| - 1, so Phi**_E = Phi*_E.

targets.author_supply_reused: The complete author Comment on physical p. 638 (printed p. 621): the failure of an exponential tail gives P[sum_{i<=n} L_i >= cn] >= P[L_1 >= cn] >= e^{-eps n} for infinitely many n; the 2^n pairwise disjoint level-n-to-level-2n paths give, by union bound, 1 - (1-e^{-eps n})^{2^n} >= 1 - exp(-e^{-eps n} 2^n) -> 1; a good path is extended to the root, giving |d_E S| / sum_{e in E(S)} L_e <= (2n+1)/(cn) ~ 2/c; and since c is arbitrary the closing display asserts the vanishing of the anchored constant a.s. This is the whole of the author's argument and it is reproduced in full.
targets.method_not_separate_target: The Comment contains one route only; there is no second author solution, so nothing is counted as an alternative target.
targets.excluded_refinement: The bookkeeping that turns "for infinitely many n" into "with probability tending to 1 there is such a path" and then into an a.s. statement along an unspecified increasing sequence of n, the count 2n+1 of boundary edges of the extended path, and the replacement of the final ratio by its limit 2/c are the author's own printed steps and are not separately counted. Nothing is added to them.
